blocks.text: But Bochart ought not to have passed over what Gesner says about the hyaena serpent in his book On Serpents, p. 59. For after relating that fable about the change of sex from Aelian and Horus, he adds: But more authors write this of the four-footed hyaena. And it is indeed uncertain whether there is any such kind of serpent, nor is it even likely that such a change of sex could be detected in it. Indeed, I cannot wonder enough that Bochart attributes so much to the futile inventions of the Rabbis that, on their authority alone, he bids the word צבוע enter the lexicons also as the name of a serpent.
